spatial_claims.claim: Points A, C, D, B are collinear in that order along line AB
C is the midpoint of AB so AC = CB
D lies between C and B
AD = AC + CD = CB + CD, i.e. AD is composed of segments CB and CD
CB = CD + DB since D lies between C and B

configuration_map: All points are collinear on a single line in the order A --- C --- D --- B. C is the midpoint of AB (AC = CB). D lies between C and B, so CD + DB = CB. The proof introduces no two-dimensional constructions — no triangles, circles, angles, or auxiliary points off the line. The entire argument is algebraic manipulation of rectangle and square area identities (Props 2.1, 2.3, 2.4) applied to segments of this line.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are about collinear point ordering on a single line (A, C, D, B in that order) and are trivially mutually consistent. The proof uses no 2D constructions, no angle decompositions, and no interior/exterior point arguments. It is purely algebraic manipulation of area identities applied to line segments, and each application (2.1, 2.3, 2.4) is valid for the established configuration.
